findings.claim: Question 2 is set as '3 marks - Describe' ('Describe what Tawhid means and why it is central to Islamic belief.'). The same 3-mark Describe question appears in lessons 2, 3, 4 and 5.
findings.truth: Paper 4 has two questions, each lettered (a) to (d): (a) 3 marks Outline three, (b) 4 marks Explain two, (c) 5 marks Explain two with a source, (d) 12 marks Evaluate. The spec command-word table gives Describe 4 marks, not 3, and this paper does not use it. Recast each as an Outline three question; the mark schemes already list three one-mark points.
findings.evidence: spec Paper 4 assessment overview (lines 432-470), assessment information (line 3715), command-word table (lines 4280-4345)

findings.claim: The 12-mark question ends 'Discuss this statement.' and is typed '12 marks - Discuss a Statement'. The same wording appears in lessons 2, 3, 4 and 5.
findings.truth: The command word for the 12-mark AO2 question in this qualification is Evaluate, not Discuss. Discuss belongs to another board. A student trained on 'Discuss' will not recognise the instruction on the paper.
findings.evidence: spec command-word table (lines 4280-4360): '*Evaluate ... 12 ... AO2'; 'Additional instructions are provided to students for all Evaluate questions'

findings.claim: 'For 12-mark Discuss questions on Tawhid or the nature of Allah...'. The same phrase appears in the exam tips of lessons 2, 3 and 5.
findings.truth: Same as F2: the command word is Evaluate.

findings.claim: Model answer quotes the source as 'Surah 55:1 (Ar-Rahman - He taught the Qur'an)'.
findings.truth: Surah 55:1 is the single word Ar-Rahman ('The Most Merciful'). 'He taught the Qur'an' is Surah 55:2. The quotation as printed attaches the wrong text to the ayah the spec prescribes for Ar-Rahman.

findings.claim: Key Fact: 'Knowing the name, meaning and surah reference is the full exam answer for the 5-mark source question.'
findings.truth: The 5-mark question needs two points explained plus one reference to a source of wisdom or authority. Three recalled facts are not a full answer, so the sentence could cost marks.
findings.evidence: spec command-word table, Explain (5 marks): 'provide understanding ... In addition, students will be required to reference one source of wisdom or authority'

findings.claim: Glossary term 'hypocrites' is defined as '...whose faith is insincere; also called hypocrites.' The same circular text sits in the data-def attribute in content_html.
findings.truth: The definition defines the word by itself. The Arabic term is munafiqun (Surah 63 is named al-Munafiqun).

findings.claim: 'Moses returned, cast down the calf and rebuked his brother Aaron for allowing it.' (given as the content of Surah 7:148-150)
findings.truth: In Surah 7:150 Musa throws down the tablets and seizes his brother by the head. He does not throw down the calf; the calf is burnt and scattered in Surah 20:97. The passage is a prescribed one, so the narrative detail must be right.

findings.claim: 'Modern Muslim scholars such as Tariq Ramadan argue that Shari'ah is best understood as an ethical framework rather than a rigid legal code.'
findings.truth: The argument is fairly reported, but Ramadan was convicted of rape and sexual coercion in Switzerland (appeal court 2024; Federal Supreme Court rejected his appeal in August 2025, making it final) and of rape in France in March 2026 (18 years, under appeal). Naming him as an authority in material for 15-year-olds is a live safeguarding and reputational risk. The sentence works without the name.

findings.claim: Ibrahim 'is described in Surah 37:109-111 ... as one who "tended always towards good deeds."'
findings.truth: Surah 37:109-111 reads: peace upon Ibrahim; thus do We reward those who do right; he was one of Our believing servants. The quoted phrase is not in the passage.

findings.claim: Key Fact: '...the debate exists and examiners award marks for acknowledging it.'
findings.truth: A fabricated examiner claim. Nothing in the spec says marks are awarded for naming the debate. State the debate; do not promise marks.
findings.evidence: spec assessment information (line 3715) and command-word table carry no such statement

findings.claim: '...but the Qur'an does not name him - this nuance earns marks at the top level.'
findings.truth: Same class of claim as F10: an invented statement about what a mark scheme rewards.

findings.claim: 'Pharaoh has a dream that no one can interpret... Pharaoh releases and honours him.' Repeated in a knowledge check and a flashcard.
findings.truth: The Qur'an calls the ruler in the Yusuf story al-malik, the King (Surah 12:43, 12:50, 12:54). It uses Fir'awn (Pharaoh) only for the ruler in Musa's time. Calling him Pharaoh imports the Genesis account into a Qur'anic textual study.
findings.evidence: quran.com/12/43 ('the King said, I dreamt of seven fat cows...'); spec 2.4

findings.claim: Surah 12 is 'the only surah of the Qur'an devoted entirely to one prophet's life'. Repeated in the conclusion, a flashcard, the glossary and a data-def.
findings.truth: The same lesson states that Surah 71 (Nuh) 'is devoted entirely to his story', which contradicts the claim. What is distinctive about Surah 12 is that it tells one prophet's story as a single continuous narrative from start to finish.
findings.evidence: internal contradiction with the Nuh section; Qur'an surah 71

findings.claim: Of Surah 12: 'The opening verse calls it "the best of stories."'
findings.truth: The phrase is in verse 3. Verse 1 is the letters Alif Lam Ra and verse 2 says it was sent down as an Arabic Qur'an.

findings.claim: Nuh 'preached to his people for 950 years (a figurative number expressing the duration of his mission)'.
findings.truth: Surah 29:14 says he lived among them a thousand years less fifty. Whether that number is literal or figurative is disputed among Muslim scholars, so stating it as figurative presents one reading as fact.

findings.claim: Yusuf's brothers 'lie to their father Jacob'.
findings.truth: The Qur'anic name is Ya'qub. The lesson's own exam tip tells students to use the Islamic names rather than the biblical ones.

findings.claim: 'Ismail is mentioned in Surah 21:5-86' (the spec's range for 2.3).
findings.truth: Ismail appears at Surah 21:85-86, so the spec's printed range 21:5-86 looks like a typing slip for 21:85-86. The lesson correctly reproduces the spec, so leave it; recorded so a later pass does not 'correct' it away from the spec.

summary: Two systematic exam-form faults run through all five lessons: a 3-mark Describe question (this paper has no such question) and the command word Discuss in place of Evaluate. Content is otherwise accurate; the substantive corrections are a misquoted Surah 55:1, the golden-calf narrative in Surah 7:150, 'Pharaoh' for the King in the Yusuf story, two invented examiner claims, and the removal of Tariq Ramadan's name.
